Very interesting Caixin article on the development of what it calls a "state-subsidized AI bubble".

The goal of recent directives, it says, "is to weed out weak, speculative, or fraudulent players by raising the barrier to entry. But in doing so, regulators have caused a fundamental reset of China’s primary market, accelerating a paradigm shift where independent venture capitalists are being squeezed out, state-backed entities are consolidating power, and policy-driven capital is generating highly concentrated tech bubbles."

When the need to keep investment growth from decelerating collides with the lack of productive investment opportunities, it is no surprise that the economy must shift from sectors the operate under hard-budget constraints to sectors that operate under soft-budget constraints.

I hope people by now realize that the general m.o. of Chinese SME companies has been to under-promise and over-deliver and generally take a conservative stance on forecasting.

Also what is reported in mainstream media — which abides by certain standards of fact-checking and vetting — is usually going to be on a lagged basis.

This is a function of the vetting process itself (which takes time to do properly) and extremely strict non-disclosure policies due to the geopolitically sensitive nature of the effort.

Many people think China exaggerates its development progress (note: popular narratives of “fake or exaggerated GDP”). Track record suggests the opposite: News getting out trumpeting China’s progress is typically viewed by authorities as harmful to national interests.

My default assumption is that what makes it into mainstream outlets is dated by around 6-12 months.

You work your ass off to get a lot of money. But what is that money actually for?

Money has no intrinsic value—it only matters if you have a clear purpose behind it. Will it get you better friends, a better marriage, or a better relationship with your kids? You better answer that question first.

To me, real success isn’t about the money. Success is knowing your nature, finding the best path through that nature, and being able to look back and say, "That was the life I wanted to have."

Credit: Sam Parr, Shaan Puri, and My First Million

#RayDalio #DefinitionOfSuccess #MoneyAndPurpose #Mindset
